summary: Abu Ubaydah referred the case of a Muslim who killed a Dhimmi in Shaam to Umar, who ruled that the man be executed if killing Dhimmis was his habit, but otherwise pay four thousand Dirhams.
notes: Only one approved theme fits well; 'justice' proposed as new.

summary: Umar wrote to a commander forbidding his men to kill Mushrikeen who had surrendered under a promise of safety, and warned that he would punish anyone who did.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence. Also holds a second report from Abu Salama. The Abu Salama here is probably Abu Salma bin Abdur Rahmaan, not Abu Salma bin Abdil Asad (who died early in the Islaam). The commander is unnamed.

summary: Anas bin Maalik recounts how Hurmuzaan surrendered at Tustar on Umar's verdict, and how Umar spared him after Zubayr confirmed Anas's report that he had been promised amnesty; Hurmuzaan then accepted Islaam and received an allowance.
notes: Anas is both narrator and participant, so tagged subject. Hurmuzaan is not the approved hurmuz (no).

summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami reports that Umar found an old, poor Dhimmi begging, excused him from jizya and fixed an allowance for him from the treasury.
Umar tells an old Dhimmi begging at the Masaajid that the state has not treated him fairly, and has an adequate allowance given to him from the public treasury.
notes: Narrator not named ('another narration').

summary: Yazeed bin Abi Maalik reports that when a Dhimmi complained that his vineyard had been ransacked, Umar found a Sahabi carrying grapes on a shield, let him go, and ordered the owner paid from the treasury.
notes: The Sahabi who took the grapes is unnamed and left out.

summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Umar ruled in favour of a Jew against a Muslim, and when the Jew praised the verdict, Umar whipped him and asked how he knew, and the Jew explained what the Torah says about judges who rule by the truth.
notes: The Jew and the Muslim are unnamed and left out.

summary: Iyaas bin Salama relates that his father Salama, struck lightly by Umar in the marketplace, was given six hundred Dirhams by Umar for his Hajj as compensation.
notes: The text says 'Hadhrat Salama'; matched to approved salama-bin-akwa because the father of Iyaas bin Salama is that Salama. Check.

summary: Abul Furaat relates that Uthmaan, having once twisted his slave's ears, asked the slave to take retribution and told him to pull harder.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence. The slave is unnamed.

summary: Naafi bin Abdul Haarith relates how Umar chased a pigeon from his shawl in a room in Makkah, the pigeon was then killed by a snake, and Umar, after asking Uthmaan and Naafi for a verdict, had a three-year-old white goat paid as compensation.
notes: Naafi is both narrator and participant in the verdict, so tagged subject. The footnote citation to Targheeb wat Tarheeb is ignored.

summary: Kulayb reports that Ali, dividing the booty won at Isfahan into seven shares, placed a piece of a single loaf on each share and had the commanders draw lots to decide who received their share first.
notes: The text says 'Hadhrat Ali'; tagged as Ali bin Abi Taalib.

summary: The narrator, the grandfather of Isa bin Abdullaah Haashimi, reports that Ali gave an Arab woman and her freed slave equal shares of grain and forty Dirhams, and when the Arab woman protested, Ali said the Book of Allaah gives the Arabs no preference over the freed slave.
notes: Only one approved theme fits. The narrator (Isa's grandfather) and both women are unnamed and left out. Isa is named only as a link in the chain.

summary: Ali bin Rabee'ah reports that Ja'dah bin Hubayrah urged Ali to rule for the one dearer to him, and Ali refused, saying he judges only to please Allaah, and lightly struck Ja'dah's chest.
notes: The narrator Ali bin Rabee'ah is not Ali bin Abi Taalib, so left as a new entry. Only one approved theme fits.

summary: Asbagh bin Nabaatah reports that Ali, seeing traders in the marketplace encroach on their spaces, ruled that the Muslim market is like a place of salaah and that whoever arrives first has his place for the day.
notes: Trailing cross-reference to an earlier chapter and OCR debris ignored. Not the approved asbagh-bin-amr-kalbi.

summary: In a lengthy report about Khaybar, Abdullaah bin Umar says that Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha estimated the Khaybar crop fairly each year despite Jewish complaints and bribes, telling them that his love for the Prophet and his hatred of them would not make him unjust.
notes: Ends with a comma after the Jews' remark, so the report may continue. The approved list has near-duplicate entries abdullaah-bin-rawaaha and abdullaah-bin-rawwaaha; used the second, which matches the text's spelling. The Jews are unnamed.

summary: Haarith bin Suwayd relates that Miqdaad bin Aswad, seeing a man beaten by the Ameer for grazing his animal against orders, brought the man before the Ameer with his sword around his neck, secured the man's right to retribution, and then said he hoped to die while Islaam is dominant.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence. Miqdaad bin Aswad is the same man as the approved Miqdaad bin Amr (also called Ibn Aswad). The Ameer and the man are unnamed.

summary: Dahhaak reports that Abu Bakr, seeing a bird on a tree, wished he were a bird that eats fruit and flies off without any reckoning, and wished he had never been a human facing reckoning.
Dahhaak bin Muzaahim reports that Abu Bakr envied a sparrow and a sheep, and said he wished he had been a hair on the body of a Mu'min rather than a human facing reckoning.
notes: Holds several separate reports in one entry (sparrow, sheep, hair on a Mu'min).

summary: Dahhaak reports that Umar wished he were a sheep that a family fattens and then slaughters and eats, and wished he had never been a human.
Aamir bin Rabee'ah reports seeing Umar pick up a twig and wish that he had been that twig, or had never been created or been born.
notes: Not the approved rabeeah-bin-ibaad.

summary: Umar says that if a caller from the heavens announced that everyone would enter Jannah except one person, he would fear that person was himself, and if the caller announced that everyone would enter Jahannam except one, he would wish to be that one.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence. Narrator not named ('another narration').

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar asked Abu Moosa Ash'ari whether he would want his deeds after the Prophet's time cancelled out so that he got neither reward nor punishment; Abu Moosa declined, and Umar said he wanted only his deeds from the Prophet's time.
Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after Umar was stabbed, he congratulated him on his leadership and its benefits, and Umar replied that he wished to leave office with neither reward nor sin.
notes: Ibn Abbaas is both narrator and speaker, so tagged subject.

summary: Another report has Ibn Abbaas tell Umar that the glad tidings of Jannah are his, given his long companionship with the Prophet and his leadership, and Umar answers that he would ransom himself with the world from the terror ahead and wishes his leadership had neither reward nor punishment.
notes: Narrator not named.

summary: Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr reports that Umar, propped up, asked Ibn Abbaas to repeat his words and then asked him to testify to them before Allaah, and Umar was very pleased with the answer.

Abdullaah bin Umar relates that Umar, in his final illness, asked to have his head placed on the ground and said he and his mother would be ruined if his Rabb did not show mercy; Miswar reports that when Umar was stabbed he said he would ransom himself from Allaah's punishment with all the gold on earth.
notes: Two reports in one entry. The first sentence is OCR-garbled and the name is missing; read as Umar. Footnote '41' is debris.

summary: Saa'ib bin Yazid reports that someone asked Umar whether it is better not to fear criticism or to examine oneself, and Umar replied that officials must not fear criticism in matters done for Allaah, while others should reform themselves and advise the officials.
notes: Saa'eb bin Yazd matched to approved saaib (Saa'ib, yes); the approved entry has no patronymic, so check. The questioner is unnamed. 'Matters pertaining to Maah' is garbled in the OCR.

summary: Aghar, from the Banu Maalik, reports that when Abu Bakr decided to appoint Umar as successor, he advised him to fear Allaah, to remember that his leadership will be presented before Allaah, and to keep the people's blood, wealth and honour safe.

Saalim bin Abdullaah bin Umar reports Abu Bakr's parting advice on his deathbed: he had appointed Umar as successor, and he told Umar to fear Allaah, that deeds are weighed by truth and falsehood, and to beware of his own self and of people's envy.
notes: OCR is garbled in places (a sentence on Umar's possible oppression and the Qur'aan citation); the sense is kept.

summary: Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit, Zaid bin Zubayd bin Haarith and Mujaahid report Abu Bakr's last advice to Umar: fear Allaah, hope in His mercy and fear His punishment, and never be deceived about deeds or give up hope in Allaah's mercy.
notes: Three narrators give one report between them.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm reports that Abu Bakr, seeing Amr bin Al Aas off to Shaam, walked beside his mount and advised him to fear Allaah, be a father to the people, guard the booty and be steadfast in battle, and keep his speech brief.
notes: OCR garbles the name of Amr's mount. Eela is a place name.

summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Abu Bakr wrote to Amr bin Al Aas and Waleed bin Uqaba, who were collecting half the Zakaah of the Qudaa'ah tribe, urging them to fear Allaah in private and in public.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('never be'). Waleed bin Uqaba is the son of Uqba bin Abi Mu'eet, who is the approved 'no' entry, so do not confuse them.

summary: Muttalib bin Saa'ib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports Abu Bakr's letter to Amr bin Al Aas about Khaalid bin Waleed, who was to reinforce him: treat him well, do not assert authority over him, and consult the others without opposing their views.

people.name: Muttalib bin Saa'ib bin Abu Wadaa'ah

summary: Abdul Hameed bin Ja'far reports that Abu Bakr appointed Amr bin Al Aas over the Baliy, Udhra, Qudaa'ah and other Arab tribes, and told him to encourage them to wage jihaad, provide for them, and treat each tribe according to its status.
notes: Trailing OCR debris ignored.

summary: Muhammad bin Ibraheem bin Haarith Taymi reports that Abu Bakr, relieving Khaalid bin Sa'eed of his post, advised Shurahbeel bin Hasanah to honour Khaalid's status and to consult Abu Ubaydah, Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Khaalid before deciding anything.
notes: The approved list has near-duplicates: muhammad-bin-ibraheem-bin-haarith (unsure) and muhammad-bin-ibraheem-taymi (no). Used the first, which matches the full name; check. Trailing citation ignored.

summary: Haarith bin Fadhl reports that Abu Bakr gave the flag to Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan and appointed him over the army in Khaalid bin Sa'eed's place, then told him to honour Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh bin Jabal, quoting the Prophet's praise of both, and never to decide without them.
notes: The Prophet's words are quoted in support of Abu Ubaydah and Mu'aadh.

summary: Yazeed bin Abu Sufyaan reports that Abu Bakr warned him not to favour his relatives in appointments, quoting the Prophet's warning that whoever appoints someone out of love for them, or gives a brother's wealth to another out of love, incurs Allaah's curse.
notes: Yazeed is both narrator and the one advised, so tagged subject. Trailing OCR debris ignored.

summary: Umar, as parting advice to his successor, urges him to honour the early Muhaajireen, recognise the good Ansaar, treat the people of other cities and the Bedouins well, take from them only their surplus, and protect the Dhimmis.
notes: No narrator named ('Hadhrat Umar once said').

summary: Qaasim bin Muhammad reports that Umar told his successor that many would seek to take the Khilaafah from him, that Umar himself had to struggle to hold off challengers, and that he would rather be executed than be appointed if someone stronger were known.

Saalih bin Kaysaan reports that the first letter Umar wrote as Khalifah gave Abu Ubaydah command of Khaalid bin Waleed's army, with instructions to fear Allaah, not to send Muslims to destruction for booty, to scout each camp, and not to be drawn to the world.
notes: The letter is given in full.
